newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Egypt envoy to brief Arafat on summit with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Egypt envoy to brief Arafat on summit with Israel.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak's adviser will arrive in Gaza on Wednesday to brief Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on results of Tuesday's Israeli-Egyptian summit, a PLO official said.
"I can tell you that Osama al-Baz is coming at 10 a.m. (0700 GMT) to see Yasser Arafat and brief him," Palestinian peace negotiator Saeb Erekat told Reuters.
A senior Israeli official said al-Baz would shuttle between Israelis and Palestinians.
Erekat said it was still early to judge if the summit between Mubarak and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and, aimed at reviving stalled peace talks, was a success or a failure.
But an aide to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said the summit had not eased the crisis in Middle East peacemaking.
Asked if the meeting between the two leaders brought about an improvement in the situation, Ahmed Tibi said: "Not at all."
"There was no commitment to halt settlements...(and) there is no change in the substance of the main issues," he told Israel's Channel Two television.
Both leaders said after their meeting in Egypt's Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh that they had taken a first step towards reviving peace talks stalled since March but more meetings were necessary.
Israel's groundbreaking on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem more than two months ago plunged peacemaking with Arafat's Palestinian Authority into crisis.
Arafat has said he will not renew talks with Netanyahu until Israel freezes construction at the East Jerusalem site.
"We need another meeting and we need more deliberation," Mubarak told a news conference after three hours of talks with Netanyahu.

Mubarak has suggested Israel halt work on the settlement, known as Har Homa or Jabal Abu Ghneim, for six months to give the peace process new momentum but neither leader would say if that or other bridging proposals were discussed.
Netanyahu referred to the meeting with Mubarak as a "positive beginning. But we need more work and we are committed to work together with you (Egypt) to achieve progress."
